title: A helpfully short history of the umbrella
text: The umbrella {{1}} invented to protect people from the sun, not the rain. Ancient civilisations {{2}} Egypt and China used parasols as symbols of power. In Europe, umbrellas were initially viewed {{3}} ridiculous, and the first man to carry one in public in London was showered {{4}} insults. Gradually, however, attitudes changed, {{5}} by the end of the eighteenth century almost everybody carried one. Umbrella manufacture became a major industry, {{6}} in the development of stronger, lighter frames. Today's folding models would have been unimaginable {{7}} those early pioneers, {{8}} inventions were heavy and awkward.

gaps.explanation: Past simple passive: the umbrella was invented.
'so' links result: attitudes changed, so by 1800 everybody carried one.
Participle clause of result: leading to the development.
'to/by those pioneers' — for them as observers; 'by' chosen for the frame.
